cells.tense: A first concrete thing is in your hand, and you are deciding whether to pick it up.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Give one concrete piece of help this week and finish it before you start anything else.
cells.core:
There's a first concrete thing here — a resource, an offer, something you could put your weight behind — and you can hold it steady without forcing it into shape. You don't need to know what it becomes. You can choose what matters and set the rest down. That steadiness is real; it's the floor under a week that could otherwise scatter.

The way back through is feeding what's around you. Give one concrete piece of help this week and finish it before you start anything else. Help that gets finished carries the strength it was meant to carry; help that gets promised and floated has already spent it. Finish the one, and the rest of the week gets its footing back.

cells.tense: A future you cannot write in is being braced against, and the first thing keeps getting set down before it is finished.
cells.act: let the felt connection be complete
cells.ask: Sit with what you already feel for someone until nothing in it is rushing, and hold off on the next move.
cells.core:
The first concrete thing keeps arriving, and the grip keeps tightening before it has landed. Something is ready to begin and the brace for what comes after is already writing the ending — the seed in your hand gets handled so hard it stops being a seed. What was meant to be chosen becomes a future being defended. The hand is doing the work the moment was supposed to do.

Sit with what you already feel for someone until nothing in it is rushing, and hold off on the next move. Knowing a feeling fully is not the same as solving it; you can put it down once you've let it finish. The first thing can be picked up again after — from a floor instead of a brace.

cells.tense: The door you were standing at has already closed behind you, and the first concrete thing still hasn't been picked up.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Spread an unmade choice across the table — every piece, no deciding yet — and keep looking until nothing is hidden.
cells.core:
Something concrete was ready to start, and it stayed where it was set down. The decision has gone quiet — not refused, just unarrived. You watch from behind the glass now, and the first thing waits on the far side of a boundary you already crossed. It's still there. Nobody moved it while you weren't looking.

Spread an unmade choice across the table — every piece, no deciding yet — and keep looking until nothing is hidden. Seeing it whole is its own kind of finish; you don't have to pick it up to step out from behind the glass. The looking pulls the current back into the hands that stopped.
cells.sheetLine: The thing you keep not choosing is still right where you set it.

cells.tense: A pen is moving under your name, and you did not sit down to write with it.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Write down the last real choice you made — not why, just what — and leave it somewhere you'll cross it again.
cells.core:
You have been steering — saying this and not that, setting things in motion and holding them — and you would not call it choosing. The direction is real; the hand on the wheel is not in your account of it. Somewhere a first thing got picked up and carried, and the motion does not show up as yours. That isn't modesty. It's a pen moving under your name, and the ink keeps arriving without you remembering picking it up.

Write down the last real choice you made — not why, just what — and leave it somewhere you'll cross it again. The small act turns the wheel back toward the one holding it. Not a method, not a habit: one line that puts the pen back in the hand that's been moving it.

The closest unsupported claim is that the Too Much cell's 'nothing gets set down' implies a pattern the record does not state; a reader could reasonably say 'I do finish things.' The sentence that serves me more than them is 'You can pick the one that matters' in the Balanced core — it flatters the seat's power rather than describing the bend; I have kept it because it is also the truest thing in the cell, and the ask releases it into action rather than leaving it as praise.
